evidence: Cic. Brut. 105: quaestiōnēs perpetuae, standing courts (Lewis & Short: “a permanent tribunal”)
terms.comment: Lasting without a break, and so permanent: snow that never melts, a standing court. It also means continuous, whole: diem perpetuum, the whole day long (Ter. Ad.); ōrātiō perpetua, a continuous speech (Lewis & Short). Permanently, for good: in perpetuum (Cic. Cat. 1.30, Lewis & Short) or perpetuō.

evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.4.107, of water that never fails (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From per annum: lasting the year round, and so of springs that never run dry, a hearth always alight, a work that endures (exēgī monumentum aere perennius, Hor. C. 3.30.1). Morgan–Owens gives it for permanent.

evidence: Verg. A. 3.86 (Lewis & Short, s.v. maneō: “lasting, permanent”)
terms.comment: What is going to stay. Tacitus sets Pompey’s theatre, a seat built to last, against the stands put up for the occasion before it (see temporary).

phrases.latin: nix jacet, et jactam nē sōl pluviaeque resolvant, indūrat Boreās perpetuamque facit
phrases.english: snow lies, and once it has fallen, so that neither sun nor rain may melt it, the north wind hardens it and makes it permanent

phrases.latin: effinge aliquid et excūde, quod sit perpetuō tuum
phrases.english: shape and hammer out something that will be yours for good

phrases.latin: rēs nōn parta labōre, sed relicta; nōn ingrātus ager, focus perennis
phrases.english: means not won by toil but inherited; land that repays you; a hearth always alight

phrases.latin: Perenne conjugium animus, nōn corpus facit.
phrases.english: A lasting marriage is made by the mind, not the body.
